name: IPOR vault admin EIP-7702 delegate executes caller-supplied calls
summary: The admin EOA 0xd8a1087d of the legacy IPOR USDC Lending Optimizer vault 0xa91267a2 on Arbitrum had delegated (EIP-7702) to Alpha's reward-compounding utility 0xa3ccb120, whose 0x64b0f06f entry point is callable by anyone and makes the account execute caller-supplied calls. The attacker called it three times: first to have the admin account call its factory 0xf38b195d, which created the fuse 0xeb0d60a1; then to run a vault execute; then to call the vault's configureInstantWithdrawalFuses (restricted to the admin, and unlike later Fusion vaults not checking that the fuse is supported) with that fuse. A 1 USDC withdrawal by its own vault position then ran the fuse, which withdrew 269,217.10 aArbUSDCn and 65,753.79 eUSDC-1 from the vault to the attacker.
notes: Cohort: no key was taken. Every attacker step is a transaction from the fresh EOA 0xeca8a633 (funded at block 418616326) to the admin EOA, executing the unverified delegate 0xa3ccb120 that the admin itself deployed (block 404736180) and delegated to; the delegate's entry point performs caller-chosen calls as the admin. The vault behaved as designed for its admin; its missing fuse-support check in configureInstantWithdrawalFuses is why one admin call sufficed, but the anchor did not execute the vault and the vault (created block 249623036, 2024-09-03) is far older than the delegation, so it is not listed.

Anchor is the defect's first successful use (rule 10): 0x8c53f7f2 made the admin account approve its ARB to and call the attacker's factory, which created the instant-withdrawal fuse 0xeb0d60a1. Three earlier attacker calls to 0x64b0f06f (0x7fe6ac6a, 0x5f4b8fc5, 0x31d30bd9) reverted. The vault execute 0x5978d042 moved 1 USDC of the vault into Aave without loss; 0x238b4e61 installed the fuse; 0x08578745 is the drain. The attacker's later 0x4c657427 call to the admin (0xf6bc208b) made no calls and moved nothing. The delegate runs as the admin EOA's own code (EIP-7702), so every log naming the admin EOA in a topic from the delegation (block 404815918) to the anchor was collected: they come only from the admin's own six self-calls of 0x64b0f06f and the attacker's three, and Arbiscan's txlist of the admin shows no other external caller.

Reset is the admin's type-4 transaction 0x6374ade7 (block 404815918, 2025-11-27) authorising delegation to 0xa3ccb120; the account had no code at the preceding block. Before it the admin only called the vault's execute directly.

Loss is the vault's depletion in the drain: 269,217.104006 aArbUSDCn sent to the attacker and 65,753.79076 eUSDC-1 Euler shares, which DefiLlama does not price and are valued at the 67,304.659866 USDC the attacker redeemed them for (0xf99d7af1, rule 12); USDC at its block price of 0.99998. loss.mjs also counts the 1.009 aArbUSDCn the vault redeemed to pay the attacker contract's own 1 USDC withdrawal, which is its deposit, not victim assets. The attacker returned 92 ETH and IPOR's DAO topped up the vault (0x7734fcc8 restored 336,580 USDC); recoveries are not subtracted (rule 11).
